correctness.rationale: For arbitrary exchangeable size-law probabilities, the one-step kernel is a convex sum of central subgroup-averaged orthogonal projections; Young branching proves each eigenvalue and regular-representation multiplicity. The proof bounds every nontrivial skew-tableau ratio by a uniform linear-extension minimal-cell injection, sharp at partition (n-1,1), giving the two-statistic gap and irreducibility condition. Exact rational direct convolution and spectral trace moment checks passed 1752 assertions for n=2 through 6; these support rather than replace the general proof.

value.rationale: For the natural repeated partial-scrambling chain motivated by recent smoothed-permutation work, all n! eigenmodes are described for every subset-size law. More surprisingly, the entire L2 gap depends only on EK and mass at K=0, despite different higher spectra. The sharp tableau domination gives a structural finite-size extremal statement useful for benchmarking partial reshuffles; no unproved mixing-time cutoff is claimed.
